source_problem: Heterogeneous context can destabilize the propagation of sequence and intent representations across depth.
reported_mechanism: Context-conditioned residual feature transport uses reliability-aware field context to control intent/sequence updates and preserve memory paths.

reported_evidence.summary: Appendix C separates transport and distillation; Appendix F reports limited or adverse effects from added capacity and longer training. These are participant-reported contrasts.
reported_evidence.locator: craft-paper-v1, Appendix C Table 9 and Appendix F
limitations: Representation diagnostics are not a causal proof.
Local matched-cost replication and seed variation are unknown.

conditions: multiple meaningful feature groups and behavioral representations exist
representation diagnostics reveal a consequential stability or information-retention issue

transfer_risks: post-click conversion and click prediction have different labels
category/brand histories have coarser identity than richer source-domain events
more gates or capacity may explain an apparent gain
possible_discriminating_checks: measure representation norms, effective rank and field dependence
compare learned contextual modulation with equal-capacity context-independent or shuffled-context controls

source_problem: Strong field signals and fragmented behavior sources can obscure useful sequential evidence.
reported_mechanism: Dual sequence paths combine older-history compression with local processing; domain summaries exchange information and feed it back through gates.

reported_evidence.summary: The organizer reports a second-place system-level result; isolated component effect sizes and detailed implementation are not established here.
limitations: Organizer summary only; original implementation and full ablation tables have not been inspected.

conditions: older and recent behaviors carry distinguishable useful information
behavior groups contain sufficient complementary observations

transfer_risks: behavior types are not interchangeable with business domains
rare actions may not support separate large branches
compression benefit may be a different input or compute budget
possible_discriminating_checks: separate history compression, local path and group exchange in controlled contrasts

source_problem: Token construction and capacity allocation can constrain field/sequence interaction.
reported_mechanism: Jointly projected fields form allocated tokens; target-aware interest tokens and gated sequence decoding connect field and behavioral representations.

reported_evidence.summary: The report describes gains over the source baseline and unequal value of token allocations; local component attribution is unverified.
limitations: Organizer summary only; original implementation and full ablation tables have not been inspected.

conditions: field groups have distinct semantics and adequate support
a bottleneck from token construction is actually observed

transfer_risks: a coarse category/brand vocabulary may erase source-domain advantages
more tokens change capacity and inference cost together
auxiliary supervision must remain inside the allowed training information
possible_discriminating_checks: replace tokenization while matching downstream capacity
compare uniform and asymmetric token budgets at measured equal cost

source_problem: Projection-only queries may insufficiently use field context when retrieving behavior evidence.
reported_mechanism: Attention generates query probes; a field-sequence bridge refines evidence, while packed shared-parameter execution supports multiple views.

reported_evidence.summary: The paper compares query-generation replacements and view scaling. Its development split is not adopted for this task.
reported_evidence.locator: queryformer-paper-v1, section 5.2 Table 4; source split in section 5.1
limitations: The source uses a row-group holdout.
Component removal changes capacity and computation; nearest equal-budget replacement remains necessary.

conditions: target-aware history retrieval is useful on the available fields

transfer_risks: category/brand matching may need less expressive queries
multiple views can increase capacity without validating the query explanation
source task and development distribution differ
possible_discriminating_checks: replace query construction with a capacity-matched projection
separate query quality from view count and shared execution savings

source_problem: Repeated nonlinear mixing may dilute explicit low-order relevance signals.
reported_mechanism: Parallel field-mixing and sequence-retrieval paths exchange state; an FM Highway sends per-layer dot-product interactions directly to the classifier.

reported_evidence.summary: Component removal is studied in tiny single-path random-holdout mode. Removing the highway hurts most; removing bus fusion improves AUC but worsens Logloss, leaving the fusion explanation unresolved.
reported_evidence.locator: unidot-paper-v1, section 5.3 Table 4 and Appendix B Table 7
limitations: Small-mode ablations do not establish identical full-scale effects.
The final recipe changes capacity, optimization and supervision together.

conditions: explicit current-ad versus history-field relevance is meaningful
a deep model loses useful direct interaction information
missing_evidence: incremental value of direct interaction readouts
cost of sequence reuse across target queries

transfer_risks: conversion-delay supervision is unavailable in ordinary click labels
auxiliary heads and optimizer changes can confound architecture gains
a smaller shallow model may already preserve the relevant signals
possible_discriminating_checks: compare highway removal with a matched extra readout head
separate per-layer interactions, depth and training recipe

Preserve the earlier count-branch decisions as historically correct for the then-available evidence.

The new factorial shows local sensitivity to explicit product choice, with favorable cross-removal performance contrasts at seed 42. This qualifies the earlier absence-of-evidence statement without establishing semantic alignment, a general field bottleneck or external novelty.

AUC interaction for cross/context removal is -0.0002827692. Context removal trades higher AUC for higher Logloss at either cross setting. Empty-history and pv-absent joint results worsen both metrics. Preserve these negative and qualified findings.

The round-3 ordinary bridge is not metrically identical to the historical DIN adaptation despite its exact-operation receipt claim: AUC -0.0000309064 and Logloss +0.0000745803. Reproduction cause unresolved; no matching-source checkpoint/prediction comparison is available.

Count-normalization negatives remain: full and half strengths lose DIN AUC; half pooling improves but remains below target-aware references. Product construction and normalization are different factors; no combination has been measured.

DIN v4 section 4.3 explicitly abandons attention softmax; the host masked-softmax reference is a DIN-style adaptation. Primary-source inspection improves provenance, not evidence of local causal truth or novelty.
